correctness.rationale: The fiber endpoint limits for the one-sided screen are supported by direct bracketing and min–max with the merged and split cross-sections; ordered eigenvalues stay continuous. The exact floor sum and Faulhaber expansion give a width-independent negative linear correction with rigorously bounded square-root remainder. Merged minus split counts thus exceed the number of labels introduced by a 2B energy shift for every energy beyond a fully explicit threshold. The j-th continuous spectral band then covers an exact length-2B interval and these tile the entire half-line. The rational polynomial identity and floor-step arithmetic were independently replayed in verify.py, while finite tests are not treated as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The natural one-sided Dirichlet interface changes from one merged magnetic layer to two split magnetic layers. Determining whether the possible spectral gaps stop at high energy is a physically and mathematically structural problem, beyond low-energy existence and generic transport. This theorem answers it for all positive field strengths and both layer widths and supplies an explicit reproducible cutoff, while carefully leaving the optimal gap count and threshold unknown.
